markdown_report:
The proposed experiment adds learned distance penalties inside existing BERT4Rec attention layers. It targets stale-history influence and broad associations displacing specific recent matches while retaining access to durable interests. These are hypotheses, not established causes of the observed errors.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Masked training and appended-mask inference provide a leakage-safe foundation, provided targets and target-derived features remain hidden. Interior targets nevertheless receive right context unavailable during terminal prediction. (2) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative margin p10 and wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These sampled training measurements motivate studying difficult rankings but cannot establish validation performance. (3) Users report stale interests and overly broad matches. Locality addresses both provisionally; recency cannot establish compatibility or present intent.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec includes last-item-only masking, making supervision alignment a credible alternative explanation [1,2]. Audit the inherited terminal/interior allocation before proposing changes. (2) KERPLE directly precedes logarithmic per-head distance penalties [3]; this proposal fixes its inner distance scale and adapts it to bidirectional recommendation. (3) TiSASRec and ScaleRec motivate temporal relationships and multiple preference scales [4,5], without proving gains here. (4) AHNS motivates moderate negative hardness [6], but unseen competitors remain uncertain negatives.

**Framework.** Four intervention axes organize the evidence: supervision alignment changes where prediction is trained; context weighting changes which observations influence it; candidate selection changes competitive pressure; content sharing transfers item evidence. Their gaps are terminal mismatch, unknown intent, uncertain negative labels, and unavailable ownership information, respectively.

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means more work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment for each dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Learned attention locality [3–5] | 2/6/6/6/6 | Originality: controlled BERT adaptation / direct KERPLE precedent. Potential: tests context reliance / intent remains unknown. User: targets stale and broad matches / specificity is indirect. Model: tests weak margins / locality cause unmeasured. Difficulty: few parameters / attention parity and backend costs. |
| Moderate-hardness curriculum [6] | 3/6/5/8/4 | Originality: controlled adaptation / close precedent. Potential: informative competition / false negatives. User: finer distinctions / no present-need signal. Model: targets misordering / sampling mismatch. Difficulty: unchanged serving / mining cost. |
| Joint title-token encoder | 4/6/6/6/7 | Originality: lightweight content sharing / established fusion. Potential: sparse-item transfer / resemblance shortcuts. User: item details / no ownership evidence. Model: richer distinctions / sparsity failure unmeasured. Difficulty: one network / substantial export integration. |
| Terminal-supervision allocation [1,2] | 2/6/6/7/3 | Originality: controlled alignment / established masking strategy. Potential: reduces mismatch / may already be implemented. User: next-choice focus / no explicit specificity. Model: terminal errors / current metrics pooled. Difficulty: sampler change / matched target counts require care. |

**Selected experiment.** At 0% progress, retain locality as one isolated intervention, after attention-equivalence checks. Each head learns a nonnegative logarithmic distance penalty. Replace the previous tiny initialization with a prespecified effective strength of 0.1; measure gradients rather than assume learning. Keep supervision allocation unchanged. A later budgeted allocation comparison remains separate.

Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Report diagnostic definitions, unavailable probes, category outcomes, runtime, and recent/older-context perturbations on training histories. Sampled gains need not transfer to full-catalog rankings [7].

idea.description: Add a learned logarithmic position-distance penalty to each attention head of the supplied corrected BERT4Rec, retaining one jointly trained network and one selected checkpoint per category. This is a restricted KERPLE-style adaptation, not a new attention formula. Test locality alone without combining negative mining, text fusion, context deletion, supervision reallocation, or loss changes.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies historical interests receiving excessive weight and broad associations outranking specific recent matches. Learned locality may reduce distant-context influence while preserving observed items and allowing heads with small penalties to retain broad attention. This explicitly addresses two reported failures, but its connection to specificity is indirect: proximity cannot establish equipment compatibility, duplication, ownership, mood, or current purpose. The model-facing target is the weak positive–negative margin tail in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics. An alternative explanation is interior-versus-terminal supervision mismatch, which must be measured rather than attributed to insufficient locality. The supplied historical scores are not controlled evidence for this intervention.
idea.implementation_notes:
The prompt contains no corrected baseline source. The code is an attention integration component, not an executable replacement train.py. It does not invent the host's data loading, constructor, sampler, checkpoint interfaces, or predictor writer. Complete reproduction requires integration into that supplied source and recording its resolved configuration.

Insert one LocalityAttention module into each existing BERT4Rec attention layer after the unchanged Q/K/V projections and before the unchanged output projection. Preserve projection weights and biases, head reshaping, embedding dimensions, normalization, residual placement, feed-forward layers, scoring head, losses, optimizer, scheduler, regularization, endpoint sampling, masking, positional convention, validation cadence, and checkpoint tie-breaking. Record these settings, terminal/interior branch coefficients, supervised target counts, and actual terminal-mask frequency. Do not presume that the corrected baseline lacks terminal supervision; BERT4Rec already includes last-item-only masking, and the supplied inspirations describe terminal/interior training.

Use b_h(i,j)=-a_h*log(1+|i-j|)/log(maxlen), with a_h=softplus(raw_h), independently learned per head and layer. This is a restricted logarithmic KERPLE form with fixed inner scale, a fixed normalization, and full absolute distance for bidirectional use. It differs from KERPLE's two learned positive parameters and published initialization; do not describe it as an exact reproduction. Keep the baseline absolute positional embeddings. Distances use original dense slot positions, including any existing PAD holes, with no compaction or reindexing. Fixed checkpoint maxlen determines normalization; runtime sequence length must not change the scale.

Prespecify effective a_h=0.1 initially by setting raw_h=log(expm1(0.1)). This replaces the previous raw=-4 initialization, whose effective strength was approximately 0.018 and whose softplus derivative was also small. The new value is an experimental choice, not a literature-validated optimum. It creates a small nonzero initial locality penalty and is not exactly baseline-equivalent. Measure finite, nonzero bias gradients and effective-strength trajectories on a fixed panel before interpreting a null result. Very weak gradients can also arise from attention or loss saturation. Do not introduce a validation-driven initialization sweep. Tiny strengths permit broadly attentive heads; the nonnegative parameterization cannot reward distance or model nonmonotonic preferences.

Do not add causal masking: visible histories and reserved MASK positions remain bidirectionally connected. PAD keys must be blocked in every layer. Padded queries must be excluded from supervision and readout; their returned attention values are zeroed by the helper. Later residuals or biases may make padded features nonzero, so zero attention outputs alone do not guarantee zero padded hidden states. Reject all-PAD rows. Terminal rows contain at least the reserved MASK.

SDPA replaces attention computation only. Preserve the original projections and output projection. Its default scale is 1/sqrt(head_dim); do not pre-scale Q again. Audit whether the baseline has custom scaling, Q/K normalization, attention masks, or other logit modifications. The helper requires standard scaling and no additional structural mask beyond padding. If the baseline differs, preserve its actual computation in the integration rather than silently adopting this helper's assumptions. Use a floating additive bias with negative infinity at PAD keys. SDPA boolean True means allowed, whereas MultiheadAttention boolean True means blocked. Match floating-mask dtype to Q/K/V and set dropout_p=0 explicitly during evaluation.

Before training locality, set an exact zero-bias control through the helper's verification flag. With dropout disabled, compare outputs, valid-query input gradients, and Q/K/V/output-projection parameter gradients against the actual baseline attention path, retaining identical weights. Compare valid-query results because the helper explicitly zeroes PAD queries. Use a fixed random linear probe over valid outputs for gradient checks. Nonzero-dropout kernels need not consume identical random masks, so dropout-disabled equivalence does not prove stochastic trajectory identity. If replacing the baseline attention implementation changes numerics or backend behavior materially, use the same integrated path with zero bias as the common control; distinguish that comparison from the historical baseline. Restore training mode and ordinary settings after checks.

Run a second fixed-panel check with locality enabled and verify finite bias gradients, finite valid-query outputs, and optimizer updates to locality_raw. Use float32 reference checks, initially atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4, reporting any justified backend-specific tolerance rather than silently loosening checks. Do not require bitwise equivalence across different attention kernels. Architectural locality changes upstream features, so matching a zero-bias implementation is necessary before attributing differences to the penalty.

Profile actual forward and backward memory and time. Dense locality preserves quadratic attention arithmetic and may materialize an O(BHL²) combined mask. An arbitrary trainable additive bias can prevent a fused backend from running; speedups are not guaranteed. Inspect the installed PyTorch/GPU behavior, optionally using sdpa_kernel to expose support restrictions, without forcing an unsupported backend in production. Record library versions, dtype, device, actual configuration, peak memory and elapsed GPU time. If the implementation cannot complete within the resource cap, report the incomplete run rather than changing batch counts, training horizon, or comparison conditions after seeing results.

Keep target construction leakage-free. For terminal examples, remove the target occurrence and all later interactions before truncating the observed prefix to maxlen-1, appending the reserved MASK, and left-padding. Interior supervised items must remain hidden under the corrected baseline's masking policy. Earlier repeated occurrences are legitimate observed context. No shifted next-item target may remain visible through bidirectional input. Use the greatest nonpadding position for serving, never nonpadding_count-1. Fixed-width appended-mask examples use features[:, -1]. This intervention uses histories only and introduces no target timestamps or metadata.

Update the canonical factory and embedded predictor writer together. Store locality_raw inside the same category state_dict. Save the architecture version, layer/head counts, maxlen, item mapping, PAD/MASK IDs, positional convention, locality formula and initialization, along with the selected checkpoint. working/predict.py must reconstruct modified attention layers and strictly load exactly one selected checkpoint per routed category. The zero-bias verification override must remain disabled during normal training and exported prediction. It is an integration-test facility, not a predictor mixture.

Verify exact saved-state identity and finite evaluation-score parity across the trained module, strict factory reload, ModelView, and exported predictor. Cover short, full-length, overlength/truncated, mixed-length and singleton histories, singleton/batch agreement, internal PAD holes, and identical candidate IDs. Use deterministic evaluation and existing ranking checks, initially with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 for float32 scores. Verify history truncation and appended MASK placement separately; numerical parity cannot establish leakage-free input provenance.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Preserve the actual trained view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces. The public diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Set view.dataset_name to the actual routed category. Evaluate margins only at valid hidden target positions using a frozen unaugmented panel, fixed negatives and separate diagnostic RNG. Preserve existing definitions and sample counts. Report terminal and interior metrics separately only when construction provenance is available; shape alone cannot identify them. Training diagnostics remain distinct from host validation.

For low-cost context-reliance diagnostics, use a frozen training-only terminal panel with seed 42 and separate RNG. Among real visible history tokens, define the recent segment as the latest min(2,n) tokens and the older segment as the remainder. Independently replace each segment with PAD while preserving slots, MASK and original positions; report changes in positive rank and positive–negative margins. Also shuffle IDs within each segment while retaining its slots. A singleton recent segment has no nontrivial shuffle; report eligible counts. Record removed-token counts because recent-versus-older deletion has unequal intervention size and cannot by itself isolate recency. Optionally compare equal-count deletion from recent and older segments only where both contain sufficient tokens. These are artificial perturbations, not alternate serving inputs or direct evidence of user intent. Use training-history-length bins 1–5, 6–20, and >20 and report counts by routed category. Do not alter the pinned evaluator to obtain validation perturbation scores.

Attention mass by distance and effective locality strengths are descriptive. Recent-versus-older perturbations offer stronger evidence of model reliance but can be affected by distribution shift, PAD patterns and correlated items. A gain concentrated in recent-sensitive cases would be consistent with the hypothesis; it would not prove behavioral causation. Long-history degradation would suggest lost durable information. Embedding scores near 0.5 indicate near-zero mean cosine similarity, not established collapse. Retain unavailable flags for gated probes and unavailable item-category breakdowns; do not fabricate product categories, reviews, ownership or compatibility labels.

Terminal-supervision allocation remains a separate alternative, potentially simpler than architecture changes. If budget permits a later prespecified comparison, independently vary locality and the terminal/interior coefficient while fixing sampler policies and reporting realized supervision counts. A 2x2 factorial can separate effects and interaction only when all arms complete with matched opportunities. It is not part of this initial locality-only proposal. Do not combine allocation changes with locality and attribute the resulting gain to either factor. No extra experiment is required merely to exhaust the available budget.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl and every existing route. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and the supplied configured epoch count capped at 200, including the SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Use one GPU. Preserve training RNG separation for diagnostic and verification panels. All training, diagnostics, integration profiling, controls and failed runs consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Prespecify resource caps and checkpoint opportunities; record actual updates, supervised targets, GPU seconds and incomplete runs. A fresh baseline control is useful only if budget permits. Never read other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

The selected trial exports one checkpoint per category, without independent score fusion, auxiliary fitted scorers, ensembles, or checkpoint averaging. Keep the host's splits, 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42 and macro HR@10 selection unchanged. Record all evaluated hypotheses and checkpoint opportunities because repeated validation selection can overfit. Historical scores do not isolate architectural effects, and one-seed findings do not establish training-seed robustness. One additional validation hit changes category HR@10 by 0.005 and macro HR@10 by 0.00125.

Sampled-metric research shows that model comparisons can reverse under full-catalog evaluation. Interpret any gain as specific to the pinned protocol. Preserve the twenty-real-training-user full-catalog qualitative diagnostic as a distinct source of evidence. Track immediate choices, deferred relevance, explicit mismatches and unidentified-item skips separately; unidentified items are not negative preference labels. Do not claim that simulator feedback establishes full-catalog HR@10 or confirms ownership and present needs.

Shortcut risks include overreliance on the latest item, repeated-item patterns, fixed-position padding, history length, and popularity correlated with recent interactions. Locality can suppress durable preferences and reinforce recent incidental purchases. Report descriptive training-frequency and history-length strata without fitting an auxiliary scorer. No hidden test files, external data, pretrained weights, unavailable ratings, review text, item prices/stores/categories, ownership labels or simulator diversity/conformity traits are introduced.

User Diagnosis Alignment: 6/10. Positive: explicitly targets stale-history influence and broad associations displacing recent specific matches. Negative: specificity is addressed indirectly, and locality cannot identify compatibility, duplication, mood or present purpose.
Model Diagnosis Alignment: 6/10. Positive: provides an isolated representation intervention evaluated against observed weak margin tails and wrong-rank rates. Negative: existing diagnostics do not establish inadequate locality, terminal performance or validation generalization.
idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


class LocalityAttention(nn.Module):
    """Attention core inside ONE existing bidirectional BERT4Rec layer.

    q, k, v: original, unscaled projected B x H x L x D tensors.
    padding_mask: B x L bool; True means PAD/key blocked.
    Keep original Q/K/V and output projections outside this module.
    Assumes standard 1/sqrt(D) scaling and padding-only structural masking.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_heads, maxlen, dropout_p,
                 initial_strength=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        if num_heads < 1 or maxlen < 2:
            raise ValueError('Invalid attention configuration')
        if not 0.0 <= dropout_p < 1.0:
            raise ValueError('Invalid attention dropout')
        if not math.isfinite(initial_strength) or initial_strength <= 0:
            raise ValueError('Initial strength must be finite and positive')
        self.num_heads = int(num_heads)
        self.maxlen = int(maxlen)
        self.dropout_p = float(dropout_p)
        # Stable inverse softplus: effective initial strength is exactly specified.
        raw = initial_strength + math.log(-math.expm1(-initial_strength))
        self.locality_raw = nn.Parameter(torch.full((num_heads,), raw))

    def forward(self, q, k, v, padding_mask, *,
                zero_bias_for_verification=False):
        if q.ndim != 4 or q.shape != k.shape or q.shape != v.shape:
            raise ValueError('Expected matching B x H x L x D projections')
        if not q.is_floating_point():
            raise ValueError('Projected features must be floating point')
        if q.dtype != k.dtype or q.dtype != v.dtype:
            raise ValueError('Q/K/V dtypes differ')
        if q.device != k.device or q.device != v.device:
            raise ValueError('Q/K/V devices differ')
        batch, heads, length, head_dim = q.shape
        if batch < 1 or head_dim < 1:
            raise ValueError('Empty attention dimensions')
        if heads != self.num_heads or not 1 <= length <= self.maxlen:
            raise ValueError('Attention configuration mismatch')
        if padding_mask.shape != (batch, length):
            raise ValueError('Expected B x L padding mask')
        if padding_mask.dtype != torch.bool:
            raise ValueError('padding_mask must be boolean')
        if padding_mask.device != q.device:
            raise ValueError('Padding mask and projections must share device')
        if self.locality_raw.device != q.device:
            raise ValueError('Move attention module to the model device')
        if bool(padding_mask.all(dim=1).any()):
            raise ValueError('Every row needs a visible token or MASK')

        positions = torch.arange(length, device=q.device)
        distance = (positions[:, None] - positions[None, :]).abs().float()
        distance = torch.log1p(distance) / math.log(self.maxlen)
        strength = F.softplus(self.locality_raw.float())
        if zero_bias_for_verification:
            # Exact baseline-equivalence check; never enable for serving.
            strength = strength * 0.0
        bias = -strength[None, :, None, None] * distance[None, None, :, :]
        bias = bias.expand(batch, -1, -1, -1)
        bias = bias.masked_fill(padding_mask[:, None, None, :], float('-inf'))

        # SDPA performs standard scaling internally; do not scale Q twice.
        # Floating masks add to scaled logits. Attention remains bidirectional.
        attended = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            q, k, v,
            attn_mask=bias.to(dtype=q.dtype),
            dropout_p=self.dropout_p if self.training else 0.0,
            is_causal=False,
        )
        return attended.masked_fill(padding_mask[:, None, :, None], 0.0)


def final_nonpadding_features(features, sequence):
    """LEFT padding and PAD holes are allowed; PAD=0."""
    if sequence.ndim != 2 or sequence.shape[1] == 0:
        raise ValueError('Expected nonempty B x L token sequences')
    if features.ndim != 3 or features.shape[:2] != sequence.shape:
        raise ValueError('Expected matching B x L x D features')
    if features.device != sequence.device:
        raise ValueError('Features and token IDs must share device')
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions[None, :].expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1
    ).amax(dim=1)
    if bool(last.lt(0).any()):
        raise ValueError('Empty sequence')
    rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)
    return features[rows, last]


# Integration specification; corrected baseline source is required.
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preserve all four category routes.
#
# Before training:
#   record the actual baseline architecture, scorer, losses, sampler,
#   terminal/interior allocation, optimization and checkpoint policy
#   insert this core between existing Q/K/V and output projections
#   disable dropout; compare exact-zero-bias outputs and valid-query
#   input/projection gradients against the original attention implementation
#   enable locality; verify finite, nonzero locality gradients and updates
#   profile actual forward/backward time, backend behavior and peak memory
#   keep any required integration repair common to the comparison arms
#
# For the locality-only trial:
#   preprocessing seed = 0; training seed = 42
#   for each supplied category:
#       initialize ONE corrected BERT4Rec with locality in each layer
#       for epoch in range(supplied_configured_epochs_capped_at_200):
#           for step in range(200):
#               batch = unchanged_family_specific_sample_batch()
#               # Hide every supervised target from bidirectional inputs.
#               # Terminal input removes target/suffix, then appends MASK.
#               loss = unchanged_masked_training_objective(batch)
#               unchanged_optimizer_update(loss)
#           unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_policy()
#       save ONE selected state_dict with complete architecture config
#       strictly reload and compare trained/ModelView/exported scores
#       preserve diagnostic APIs, frozen panels, definitions and availability
#
# working/predict.py must reconstruct the modified architecture exactly.
# Appended-mask serving uses final nonpadding features, never count-1.
# Verification zero-bias override stays disabled during training and serving.
# Preserve one GPU, trial-local artifacts and the shared GPU-second budget.
# Select solely through the unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10.
# No checkpoint reuse, averaging, independent score fusion or hidden labels.
# This component does not implement missing baseline infrastructure.

originality.positive: An isolated, bidirectional BERT4Rec adaptation with explicit padding, supervision and export controls can provide useful attributable evidence.
originality.negative: KERPLE directly establishes learned logarithmic distance penalties; the proposed fixed-inner-scale form and recommendation application do not establish a new attention principle.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result can clarify whether context weighting merits further study and distinguish it from supervision alignment before adding timestamps or content.
future_potential.negative: The locality mechanism is unverified, monotonic decay can lose durable preferences, and sampled validation gains need not improve full-catalog choices.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one parameter per head per layer and requires no additional dataset, pretrained encoder, independently fitted model or serving-time mining.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires attention output and gradient equivalence, careful scaling and padding, backend profiling, diagnostic adaptation, and consistent strict checkpoint reconstruction in the embedded predictor.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and appended-mask next-item inference.
Includes last-item-only masking to address differences between interior reconstruction and next-item prediction.
limitations: Does not establish that insufficient attention locality causes the supplied recommendation failures.
The inherited corrected baseline's actual terminal-supervision allocation must be audited before proposing an allocation change.

related_work.title: Recency-sampling research for sequential recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary identifies alignment concerns between random masking and next-item prediction.
Motivates supervision allocation as a separate explanation and experimental direction.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the proposed locality penalty on the pinned four-category benchmark.
Recency-sensitive training does not reveal compatibility, ownership or present intent.

related_work.title: KERPLE: Kernelized Relative Positional Embedding for Length Extrapolation
contributions: Direct prior art for learned head-specific logarithmic distance penalties of the form -r1*log(1+r2*d).
Provides the closest methodological reference for the proposed restricted logarithmic bias.
limitations: The reported setting concerns language-model length extrapolation rather than recommendation accuracy.
The proposed experiment fixes the inner scale, normalizes by log(maxlen), uses a different initialization and applies full bidirectional distances; it is not an exact reproduction.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models positional and time-interval relationships in sequential recommendation.
Motivates separating position-only locality from timestamp-dependent extensions.
limitations: Its causal backbone and interval-aware mechanism differ from this bidirectional position-only experiment.
Does not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: ScaleRec (2025)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes learned Gaussian locality and aggregation across preference scales.
Motivates retaining older interactions while learning different context scales.
limitations: The proposed monotonic logarithmic penalty is not a reproduction of its Gaussian mechanism or aggregation architecture.
The supplied evidence does not validate this adaptation under the required protocol.

related_work.title: AHNS: Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling for Collaborative Filtering
contributions: Motivates adapting negative hardness rather than always selecting extreme competitors.
Supports candidate selection as a separate intervention addressing weak ranking separation.
limitations: Transfer from collaborative filtering to masked sequential recommendation remains uncertain.
High model score does not establish that an unseen item is irrelevant.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled rankings can yield model comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog rankings.
Supports restricting claims to the pinned sampled-candidate protocol.
limitations: Does not justify changing the required evaluator.
Does not determine whether this particular intervention will change relative performance under full-catalog evaluation.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Documents projection behavior, attention masking and optimized attention paths.
Supports preserving projections, scaling and mask semantics when integrating a new attention core.
limitations: Documentation does not establish numerical equivalence to the unavailable host baseline.
Installed-version behavior and actual baseline customizations require integration checks.

related_work.title: PyTorch scaled_dot_product_attention documentation
contributions: Documents additive-mask semantics, default scaling, evaluation dropout requirements and backend-dependent numerical behavior.
Supports explicitly disabling attention dropout during evaluation and matching mask dtype to projected features.
limitations: Arbitrary trainable additive bias is not guaranteed to use a fused backend.
API correctness alone does not establish output, gradient or exported-predictor parity.

related_work.title: PyTorch scaled dot product attention tutorial
contributions: Describes backend selection and profiling tools for SDPA.
Supports measuring forward and backward costs rather than assuming acceleration.
limitations: Backend eligibility depends on hardware, installed software, tensor shapes, masks, dtype and gradient requirements.
Dense locality bias retains quadratic attention arithmetic and can increase memory or trigger backend fallback.

related_work.title: KERPLE reference implementation
contributions: Provides the supplied reference for learned logarithmic parameters, their initialization and positivity constraints.
Highlights that causal distance construction must be adapted for bidirectional attention.
limitations: The proposed single-strength softplus parameterization and initialization differ from this implementation.
Implementation precedent does not establish effective gradient magnitudes or recommendation gains in the host environment.
